summary: A red-shingled octagonal timber tower above La Martre on the Gaspé coast, lit in 1876, rebuilt 1906, with its clockwork Fresnel lens still turning for visitors.

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: mainly Lighthouse Friends (modern, copyrighted; paraphrased) plus the heritage statement and one Marine report. The Parks Canada DFHD page did not load, so the 2025/2026 heritage lighthouse date is unresolved: French Wikipedia (leads only) says 22 Sept 2025, the Lighthouse Directory says January 2026. Lighthouse Friends's claim that Leclerc was ousted because of the 1912 election is its own account; not confirmed in an official report. The story spells Louis-Philippe as in the usual form; Lighthouse Friends prints Louis-Phillipe. The 1909 report's fiscal-year coverage was not checked (report labelled 1909). Owner differs: Lighthouse Directory says CCG; the record says the municipality. Marine reports 1918-1924 list 'Riviere a la Martre' in tables with figures (175-260 etc.) not understood; not used. First-tower height 64 ft from Lighthouse Friends only. Verifier 2026-10-27: Marine report is fiscal year 1908-9 (stated in the report). Removed unsourced 'La Haute-Gaspésie'; corrected Caron's appointment wording to the source's 'Liberal MP'.
